name: Electropellers
summary: In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle wants his lost electropellers back. A mishap with an explosive duck decoy scattered the prototype parts in freshwater streams.

sections.title: A Tipsy Invention
sections.body: Wizbang Cranktoggle went inland one evening to find a place to test his latest invention. The gnome tinkerer, based in Auberdine, had built a self-propelled duck decoy that explodes. He drank too much and blacked out. Hours later, he woke in town with singed hair and an empty pack; his bag of electropellers had fallen into one of the coastal rivers.

sections.title: Dredging the Waters
sections.body: Wizbang asks local fishermen to dredge Darkshore's freshwater streams, for he will not brave the wilds himself. Anglers on the Wildbend River and Cliffspring River can snag the buoyant metal parts along with local fish. Once the components are back, Wizbang can resume his erratic waterfowl experiments.

faq.q: Where do I find the electropellers?
faq.answer: Fish in Darkshore's freshwater rivers and lakes, including the Cliffspring River and Wildbend River. The electropellers are not in the ocean along the coast.
Wizbang Cranktoggle is an eccentric gnomish engineer who lives in Auberdine. He makes bizarre, explosive inventions and relies on travelers to gather lost components and oddities for his experiments.

faq.q: What was Wizbang trying to build?
faq.answer: Wizbang was building a self-propelled duck decoy that explodes. After drinking too much, he accidentally detonated an early prototype, scorching his hair and losing his bag of parts in the water.

faq.q: Can electropellers be found in fish schools?
faq.answer: No. Electropellers come from open freshwater casts, not special schools such as Lesser Oily Blackmouth nodes.
Complete Gaffer Jacks first. Wizbang assigns it earlier to test your angling luck in the local waters.
No. Enemies and ground containers do not yield electropellers. Retrieve them from rivers with a fishing pole.

angles.text: As a gnome, you may recognize Wizbang's chaotic ambition to build exploding duck decoys. Losing expensive parts in an elf-guarded river is embarrassing.
As an engineer, you can see electropellers as curious examples of miniaturized gnomish propulsion. They drive mechanical decoys before violently combusting.
As a night elf, you may regard Wizbang's loud, smoky inventions and river-littering mishaps with quiet disapproval. Darkshore's streams should remain natural.
